_readme: THE GOOGLE PLAY DATA SAFETY DECLARATION — Subly, channel `android-play`.
This is the repo-native source of truth for the Data safety form. The Play Console is a COPY of
it, exactly as [10]D-5 already says of the listing text. Enforced by
tooling/ci/assert-play-declarations.mjs, and required to be present and non-empty by
tooling/channel-register.json -> storeMetadataContract.perChannel['android-play'].additionalFiles,
which also makes tooling/release/submit-play.mjs refuse to walk without it.
🔴 WHY THIS IS A GUARDED ARTEFACT AND NOT A FILLED-IN FORM. The Data safety section is a SWORN
DECLARATION ABOUT WHAT THE CODE DOES. Google's own User Data policy: 'All developers must complete
a clear and accurate Data safety section for every app detailing collection, use, and sharing of
user data. The developer is responsible for the accuracy of the label' (see `sources` below). A
declaration that is true the day it is typed and false three commits later is the failure mode —
and it is silent, because nothing in a store console watches a repository. So every answer that
can be DERIVED from the tree is derived, and every answer that cannot is marked as a human's to
own, by name.
🔴 THE ANSWER DEPENDS ON WHICH ARTEFACT SHIPS, AND THAT IS DERIVED, NOT ASSUMED. See
`buildPosture`. The .aab lane in .github/workflows/build-platforms.yml passes ONE dart-define
(GLITCHTIP_DSN). AppConfig.isSupabaseConfigured / isApiConfigured / isBackendLive are COMPILE-TIME
constants over those defines (apps/subly/lib/core/app_config.dart:278-301), so the bundle
Play would receive today runs MockAuthRepository, SeedApiClient and NoOpAnalytics, shows no
consent prompt, and makes exactly one kind of outbound request: a crash report. Every answer is
therefore recorded TWICE — once per posture — and the guard reads the workflow to decide which
column is the one to type into the console. Adding an identity dart-define to that lane FAILS THE
BUILD until this file is updated, which is the whole point.
🔴 `null` IS A REAL ANSWER HERE AND IT MEANS 'NOBODY KNOWS YET'. It is NOT filled with a plausible
value: a confidently wrong Data safety declaration is worse than an obviously incomplete one, and
this repository has already deleted one invented compliance number for firing on correct input. The
guard PRINTS every null on every run and says out loud that the form cannot be submitted while one
remains. `unresolved` is currently EMPTY and the form is submittable.
📌 THE TWO THAT WERE OPEN WERE BOTH SETTLED ON 2026-08-04, and both had been recorded as needing
something they did not need — see `resolved`, which keeps the write-ups rather than deleting them.
The device-identifier question was marked 'not derivable from source, because the payload is
assembled inside the vendored SDK' and prescribed a live crash against GlitchTip; the vendored SDK
is source, it is pinned in pubspec.lock, and reading it answered the question. The edge-geo question
was marked 'no primary source found'; the ruling sentence was a Note on the very page this file
already cited for its category list. BOTH FAILURES WERE THE SAME FAILURE — treating a source as
exhausted — which is why each answer now carries its own citation and its own version pin.
⚠️ NOT LEGAL ADVICE AND NOT WRITTEN BY A LAWYER — the same disclaimer tooling/legal/README.md
carries. Rows record what this repository can OBSERVE.

_why: 🔴 EVERY EXTERNAL REQUIREMENT CARRIES A URL AND A FETCH DATE, and the guard refuses a citation
whose host is not in `allowedHosts`. Same rule as tooling/legal/duty-matrix.json: the test a host
passes is that it is the body that WROTE the rule or the platform that ENFORCES it. A blog post
summarising Play policy cannot be re-verified later, and a compliance corpus is worth exactly its
ability to be re-checked.

vocabulary.quote: Play's Data safety form enumerates the data categories and the types under each: Location (Approximate location, Precise location); Personal info (Name, Email address, User IDs, Address, Phone number, Race and ethnicity, Political or religious beliefs, Sexual orientation, Other info); Financial info (User payment info, Purchase history, Credit score, Other financial info); Health and fitness; Messages; Photos and videos; Audio files; Files and docs; Calendar; Contacts; App activity; Web browsing; App info and performance (Crash logs, Diagnostics, Other app performance data); Device or other IDs.

collectedDefinition.quote: Collected = 'Transmitting data from your app off a user's device'. It includes data sent by libraries and SDKs and pseudonymous data; it EXCLUDES data processed only on the device.

sharedDefinition.quote: Shared = 'Transferring user data collected from your app to a third party'. It EXCLUDES transfers to a service provider processing on the developer's behalf.

inferredLocation.quote: Approximate location: 'User or device physical location to an area greater than or equal to 3 square kilometers, such as the city a user is in, or location provided by Android's ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION permission. Note: Approximate location that is inferred, such as via IP address or Access Point Name, must be disclosed here.'

ipAddressUsage.quote: 'How should I treat the collection and use of IP addresses? As with other data types, you should disclose your collection, use and sharing of IP addresses based on their particular usage and practices. For example, where developers use IP addresses as a means to determine location, then that data type should be declared.'

declaredFieldsPerType.quote: Per data type a developer declares: whether it is collected, shared, or both; whether it is processed ephemerally ('Accessing and using it while only stored in memory and retained no longer than necessary to service the specific request in real-time'); whether collection is required or optional ('Optional = users have control over its collection and can use the app without providing it'); and the purposes, from: App functionality, Analytics, Developer communications, Advertising or marketing, Fraud prevention security and compliance, Personalization, Account management.

dataSecurityQuestions.quote: The Data security block asks 'Whether or not all of the user data collected by your app is encrypted in transit' and 'Whether or not you provide a way for users to request that their data is deleted', plus two optional badges: 'Committed to follow the Play Families Policy' and 'Independent Security Review'.

accuracyRule.quote: User Data policy: 'All developers must complete a clear and accurate Data safety section for every app detailing collection, use, and sharing of user data. The developer is responsible for the accuracy of the label'; the section 'must be consistent with the disclosures made in the app's privacy policy' and must include data shared by integrated SDKs.

accountDeletionRule.quote: Apps that allow users to create an account must provide both an 'in-app path to delete their app accounts and associated data' and a 'web link resource where users can request app account deletion and associated data deletion'; the web link is submitted in the Data safety form, must be functional, must reference the app or developer name, and the deletion pathway 'should be prominently featured and easily discoverable on the page'. Data may be retained 'for legitimate reasons such as security, fraud prevention or regulatory compliance' if users are clearly informed.

_why: 🔴 PLAY'S OWN CATEGORY/TYPE LIST, AS STRUCTURE RATHER THAN PROSE. `sources.vocabulary` carries the
URL, the fetch date and the sentence; this is the same thing in a shape a guard can quantify over.
The two exist separately on purpose: this repository has a recorded bug where a check matched the
COMMENT explaining why a thing did not exist, so a guard that satisfied itself by finding 'Precise
location' inside a quoted paragraph would be that bug again. Every key below must have exactly one
answer row and every answer row must name a type below — both directions, so neither a forgotten
question nor an invented Play data type can pass.
⚠️ IT IS A SNAPSHOT OF A PAGE GOOGLE CAN EDIT. `sources.vocabulary.fetched` is the date it was true;
nothing in CI can notice Play adding a type, and the guard says so out loud rather than implying the
list is self-maintaining.
🔴 A ZERO NOBODY DECLARED IS A ZERO NOBODY IS ACCOUNTABLE FOR. "Advertising or marketing" is in the
vocabulary above and is used by NO answer row — which was true, unremarked and unchecked until
2026-08-09. Nothing recorded that the zero was deliberate, so nothing could tell it apart from a row
somebody forgot to tick, and the day a promo surface targets on a collected data type the purpose would
arrive on that row with no guard reading it as an advertising claim at all.
It is declared here, counted by tooling/ci/assert-ads-declarations.mjs, and compared to
apps/subly/store/android-play/ads-declaration.json — which derives the SAME answer from format rather
than from packages. Three Play advertising questions, one derivation, no second opinion.
advertisingPurpose.basis: No data type is collected for advertising or marketing. There is no ad SDK, no attribution SDK, no advertising identifier and — the half no dependency can prove — no promotional surface anywhere in the widget tree and no armed promotional lever in the served config. The format-keyed derivation lives in ads-declaration.json; this row is the Data safety form's half of the same question, and the two are compared on every run.

_why: 🔴 REQUIRED_COVERAGE FOR THE `clientAbsence` LIMB, because the limb protects a claim that is INVISIBLE
once it stops being checked. The ordinary `tells` limb only evaluates rows answering 'never collected in
any posture' — so the instant a row answers `true` (or `null`) for one posture, its entire tell list goes
quiet while still sitting in the file looking exactly like coverage. That was not hypothetical: 24 tells
across four rows were in that state when this block was written, including every location tell.
`clientAbsence` is the claim that survives collection — 'this data type is collected, but the DEVICE
still contributes nothing to it' — and it is evaluated on every run regardless of the answer. The names
below are the rows where that sentence is load-bearing, and a row listed here with no `clientAbsence`
block FAILS THE BUILD. Without this list the block could simply be deleted and the guard would go quiet
in exactly the way it exists to prevent.
⚠️ THE LIST IS ITSELF DELETABLE, and that limit is stated rather than implied. What it cannot lose
silently is a row: the guard refuses an empty list, and the general dead-tells rule (a `tells` block on a
collected row is an assertion that can never fire) catches the other direction without any list at all.
types: Device or other IDs|Device or other IDs

_why: 🔴 THIS BLOCK IS WHY THE GUARD CAN BITE AT ALL. Every answer below is a claim about an ARTEFACT,
and which artefact Play receives is decided by one line in one workflow.
apps/subly/lib/core/app_config.dart:278-301 gates the whole app on compile-time constants:
isSupabaseConfigured := SUPABASE_URL != placeholder && SUPABASE_ANON_KEY != ''
isApiConfigured      := API_BASE_URL   != placeholder
isBackendLive        := isSupabaseConfigured && isApiConfigured
and the app branches on them at four places that decide everything this form asks about:
providers.dart:540-545        isBackendLive ? SupabaseAuthRepository : InMemoryAuthRepository
providers.dart:1469           !isApiConfigured -> SeedApiClient (in-memory, never leaves the device)
analytics_providers.dart:235  !isBackendLive (via analyticsEnabledProvider) -> NoOpAnalytics
app.dart:396                  the consent prompt shows only when analyticsEnabledProvider is true
⚠️ THOSE FOUR LINE NUMBERS WERE RE-MEASURED 2026-08-10 AND THREE OF THEM WERE WRONG — the two
providers.dart citations were ~500 and ~1300 lines out (they predate the P2.6 re-stamp), the
auth fallback had been renamed MockAuthRepository -> InMemoryAuthRepository, and the fourth named
features/consent/consent_prompt.dart, a file deleted that same day with the unmounted ConsentGate.
A sworn record pointing at lines nobody has read since the re-stamp is the failure mode to watch
for here: the CLAIMS above were all still true, which is exactly why nothing went red.
✅ AND THE REPAIR IS NO LONGER A NOTE. The first version of this paragraph ended 'Re-walk these
four before any submission that follows a refactor of providers.dart or app.dart' — and that
instruction lasted less than a day: the next edit to app.dart's consent gate moved the fourth
citation from :376 to :396. assert-sworn-store-files.mjs limb 8 now reads the numbers OUT OF THIS
FILE and checks that each cited line still contains the construct it describes
(InMemoryAuthRepository() · SeedApiClient() · core.NoOpAnalytics() · const _ConsentPrompt()). It
failed the build on that :376 the moment it was written, which is how the number above got fixed.
Change any of these four constructs and the guard tells you which citation to move.
So a build with none of the identity defines COLLECTS ALMOST NOTHING, and a build with them
collects an account, user-entered finances and consented analytics. Same commit. Same source.
Two completely different Data safety forms.
⚠️ THE PLAY LANE WAS `demo` AND BECAME `backend-live` ON 2026-08-04, and this block is how that
was noticed rather than shipped. It is not an opinion — `expectedDefines` is compared to the
dart-defines on the `flutter build appbundle` step, parsed out of the workflow. The prediction
written here was 'add SUPABASE_URL there and this file becomes a lie'; somebody did exactly that
the day after, to fix a SEPARATE defect (the Play artefact was building in demo mode with mock
auth and seeded data, which is its own reason an upload would have been wrong), and this guard
failed the build naming all three identity defines. The declaration was re-pointed at the
`backend-live` column in the same change.
🔴 THE CONSEQUENCE, STATED RATHER THAN BURIED: under `demo` the two open questions below were
answerable as `false` because NoOpAnalytics sent nothing at all. Under `backend-live` they are
genuinely UNRESOLVED, so this form CANNOT BE SUBMITTED until somebody observes them. That is not
a regression introduced by the live lane — it is the real question arriving, on the day the
artefact started collecting.
buildPosture._definesNote2026_08_08: APP_VERSION and RELEASE_CHANNEL added when build-platforms.yml began threading the release line into store artefacts ([9]R-2 residual). Checked against every answer in this form before declaring: APP_VERSION is the app's own version string compiled in for crash/release attribution — the same define the web lane has shipped since deploy-web.yml existed, no data-category change. RELEASE_CHANNEL selects which first-party update-source config key the app reads ([9]R-10, owner decision #19) — no new collection, no new sharing, no third party. Neither define alters any dataSecurity answer above.

postures.demo: No identity dart-defines. MockAuthRepository, SeedApiClient (in-memory list, lost on restart), NoOpAnalytics, no consent prompt, no account. The ONLY outbound traffic is the crash rail, because GLITCHTIP_DSN is passed.
postures.backend-live: SUPABASE_URL + SUPABASE_ANON_KEY + API_BASE_URL all supplied. Real account, subscriptions/budget/payment rows synced to services/subly-api, consent-gated first-party analytics to services/platform. This is the posture .github/workflows/deploy-web.yml builds, and — since 2026-08-04 — the posture EVERY store lane builds: both Android steps, both Windows steps and both Apple steps were passing no identity defines at all, so every store artefact in the tree was the demo build. tooling/ci/assert-store-build-config.mjs now derives the required set from AppConfig.isBackendLive and grades every build step a `kind: store` row declares.

clientAbsence.claim: The DEVICE never provides a location. The only geo that exists anywhere is inferred at the Cloudflare edge from the connection, which is why this row is `collected` but `required: false` and purpose Analytics only. If any tell below appeared, that sentence would become false in the most consequential way available — the collection would be DEVICE location, `required` would have to be reconsidered, the purposes would change, and the Precise location row beneath would very likely have to flip too.

answers.basis:
🔴 SETTLED 2026-08-04 AGAINST A PRIMARY SOURCE THAT WAS ON THE PAGE THIS FILE ALREADY CITED. This answer was `null` on the recorded ground that 'no primary source answering this was found'. The statement exists, in the Approximate location row of the data-types table at support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/10787469 — the SAME URL `sources.vocabulary` already quotes — and it is explicit: 'Note: Approximate location that is inferred, such as via IP address or Access Point Name, must be disclosed here.' The FAQ further down the same page adds: 'where developers use IP addresses as a means to determine location, then that data type should be declared.' See sources.inferredLocation and sources.ipAddressUsage. The lesson is recorded rather than quietly fixed: the page had been fetched and quoted for a DIFFERENT paragraph, and a citation already in the file was treated as exhausted.

WHAT THIS APP ACTUALLY DOES. The client transmits no location — see `clientAbsence`, which is asserted on EVERY run precisely because this row is no longer 'never collected' and its tells would otherwise stop being evaluated. The geo is derived at the edge and then RETAINED: services/platform/src/routes/events.ts:117-126 reads country/region/city off `request.cf`; lines 254 and 288-290 bind them into the events INSERT; services/platform/migrations/0002_analytics.sql:47-50 declares them as columns. Derived-and-discarded would have been a different answer — that is the distinction the question turned on — but this is derived-and-stored, which is why `ephemeral` is false. City granularity sits squarely inside Play's definition ('an area greater than or equal to 3 square kilometers, such as the city a user is in').

OPTIONAL, and that is enforced upstream rather than claimed here: a geo only exists on a row, and a row only exists for a CONSENTED analytics event. Consent defaults OFF (ConsentStatus.unknown is the launch state and is not consent) and the app is fully usable without it, which is Play's own test for optional. ANALYTICS ONLY — no other route stores geo; the consent-artifact INSERT at events.ts:363 takes no geo columns. NOT SHARED: Cloudflare is a service provider processing on our behalf, which Play's `shared` definition excludes.

FALSE under demo because NoOpAnalytics posts no event at all, so no row exists for a geo to be written onto. ⚠️ ONE RESIDUAL, STATED RATHER THAN BURIED: the crash rail is on in BOTH postures, and whether the self-hosted GlitchTip instance runs its own GeoIP over the connecting address is a property of that deployment, not of this repository — it is listed in the guard's CANNOT-SEE output. It cannot change the value typed into the console, because buildPosture.current is `backend-live`, where this row is already true; it could only ever move the demo column, which is not the shipping one.

No precise location is available to any code path. The edge geo that makes the row above `null` is city-level at best and is never a device fix; services/platform/migrations/0002_analytics.sql:20-22 records that the events table has no ip column, ever.

Subly's sign-up is email and password only (apps/subly/lib/features/auth/login_screen.dart) — there is no name field anywhere in the app, and packages/core/lib/src/auth/auth_models.dart carries id and email and nothing else. ⚠️ platform_db.provider_notifications DOES hold a buyer's name verbatim, and it is excluded here rather than ignored: see `inventory.notFromThisApp` — that row is written by a merchant-of-record webhook arriving server-to-server from the provider, not by anything transmitted from this app, which is what Play's `collected` definition is about.

clientAbsence.claim: The address is TYPED BY THE USER into a sign-in form. The app never reads the device's account list, so the only address it can ever hold is one somebody deliberately entered. If GET_ACCOUNTS appeared, the app could harvest addresses the user never typed, and `required: true` for Account management would stop describing what actually happens.

answers.basis: Under backend-live the address is sent to Supabase GoTrue on sign-in, sign-up and password reset, and the session it returns is held on device under the key `nikatru.auth.session` in OS-backed secure storage. REQUIRED, because there is no way to use an account without one. NOT SHARED: Supabase is a service provider processing on our behalf, which Play's own definition excludes from `shared`. Under `demo` MockAuthRepository (providers.dart:45-50) never opens a socket, so the address never leaves the device. ⚠️ The address is never attached to an analytics event or a crash report: packages/core/lib/src/analytics/analytics.dart:64-90 caps params to enumerable scalars, and packages/telemetry/lib/src/pii_scrubber.dart redacts email addresses out of every crash surface it reaches.

The Supabase `sub` (a UUID) keys every row this app writes server-side, and travels on every request inside the bearer JWT. Required — it is the account. Not shared; Cloudflare and Supabase are service providers. Under demo there is no account and SeedApiClient never leaves the device.
No postal-address field exists in the app; grep of every TextEditingController in apps/subly/lib returns exactly five inputs (subscription name, price, email, and two passwords).
No phone field, no phone permission, no telephony package. Auth is email/password only.
No such field exists in any screen, model or migration in the tree.
No such field exists in any screen, model or migration in the tree.
No such field exists in any screen, model or migration in the tree.

The user-entered content this app holds is subscription names and prices, declared under App activity > Other user-generated content and Financial info > Other financial info rather than here, so that it is declared once and in the most specific place. No other personal field exists.

🔴 NO CARD, BANK OR ACCOUNT NUMBER IS STORED ANYWHERE, and that is already an asserted claim rather than a belief: tooling/legal/policy-claims.json carries it and assert-policy-claims.mjs checks it against every migration in the tree. subly_db.payment_history holds a date and an amount the USER recorded against their own subscription — a record OF payments, not a payment instrument. Since P2.4b (2026-08-08) Subly DOES carry the first-party client rail (nikatru_purchases — see the Purchase-history row below, flipped in the same commit), but that changes nothing in THIS row: the rail reads entitlement state and contains no checkout — payment happens on the apex web page ([ADR 038]) in a browser, so no payment instrument ever enters or transits the app. The RevenueCat tombstone (apps/subly/pubspec.yaml:123-131, updated with the same commit) records why no billing aggregator will reintroduce one.

clientAbsence.claim: Purchase EXECUTION never happens on the device. There is no Play Billing, no billing SDK and no payment form in this codebase — checkout is the apex web page ([ADR 038]) in a browser, and what the app itself does is READ entitlement state (the subscription this account holds) from the platform Worker via nikatru_purchases over the declared api_client transports. If any tell below appeared, that sentence would be false: collection would become on-device purchase execution, `shared` would need rework (a billing SDK is a third party), and the User-payment-info row above would very likely flip too.

answers.basis: FLIPPED (backend-live only) 2026-08-08 with productization P2.4b, in the SAME commit that made nikatru_purchases a dependency — this row's tells named that package in advance precisely so the dep and the answer could never move separately (the 2026-08-0x sentence 'packages/purchases is deliberately not a dependency' expired with the [ADR 036] freeze dissolution). What backend-live collection means here: the app fetches this account's entitlement/subscription state from platform_db.entitlements — a record OF this app's own subscription, keyed to the User ID, used to unlock features (App functionality; required false because the free tier works signed-out). At the time of the flip the package has ZERO call sites (first caller: the chassis money surfaces, P2.6a; paywall flip: Phase 4), so this column leads the code by design rather than trailing it. And it is the column that COUNTS: assert-play-declarations derives the lane posture from build-platforms.yml as backend-live (its own output, this same commit), so this flip DOES change what the console form would say — deliberately, in the only safe direction (a label may over-state collection; under-stating is the enforcement case), and the submission itself stays owner-gated at A-3. The purchases the USER TYPES IN about other companies' services remain user-generated content, declared elsewhere — that half of the old basis survives.
No such field, no credit-bureau integration, no such column in any migration.

DECLARED ON THE WIDE READING ON PURPOSE. What the user enters is the cost and billing cycle of services they subscribe to, plus an optional monthly budget and per-category caps. Play's 'Other financial info' is open-ended ('any other financial information'), and a recurring-spend total is a fact about somebody's money. Under backend-live these rows are transmitted to services/subly-api and stored in subly_db keyed on user_id. REQUIRED, because entering a subscription is the app. Under demo they live only in SeedApiClient's in-memory list (apps/subly/lib/data/api/seed_api_client.dart:12-13) and are lost on restart — never written to disk, never transmitted, so not `collected` under Play's own definition.
No health permission, package or entitlement anywhere in the tree.
No activity-recognition permission, no fitness package, no motion usage key.

🔴 THE APP READS NO MAILBOX, AND THE COPY THAT SUGGESTED OTHERWISE WAS ALREADY REMOVED. apps/subly/lib/features/scan/scan_screen.dart:19-28 records why: the scan screen's labels once said 'Scanning inbox receipts' and 'Reading bank statements' and were changed on 2026-07-27 because 'the app does NONE of those: there is no bank or mail integration anywhere in the dependency graph'. The screen is a Timer.periodic over five fixed strings. The EMAIL ADDRESS a user signs in with is declared under Personal info > Email address; that is an identifier, not a message.
No SMS permission and no SMS package. There is no OTP-by-SMS path — auth is email/password and magic link.

Subly is single-user. There is no chat, comment, share or any other user-to-user surface: every route in services/subly-api is scoped to the caller's own user_id and there is no route that reads another user's rows. Local renewal reminders are generated on-device by flutter_local_notifications and are not messages between people.
No media permission, no picker package, no photo-library usage key. The app has no image input of any kind.
No video permission, no camera or video package, no camera usage key.
No microphone permission, no recording or speech package, no microphone usage key.
No audio-media permission and no audio package in apps/subly/pubspec.yaml.
Same evidence as Music files: no audio-media permission and no audio package.

No storage permission, no file-picker or share package, and no direct path_provider dependency — the app performs no file I/O of its own. The Settings 'Export data (CSV)' row is an INERT placeholder with a null onTap (apps/subly/lib/features/settings/settings_screen.dart), so nothing is written or read.

⚠️ SUBLY HAS A SCREEN CALLED 'CALENDAR' AND IT IS NOT THE OS CALENDAR. apps/subly/lib/features/calendar/calendar_screen.dart renders a month grid of the app's OWN subscription renewal dates. No calendar permission, no calendar package, no calendar usage key — the OS calendar is never read or written.
No contacts permission, no contacts package, no contacts usage key.

clientAbsence.claim: Analytics here is FIRST-PARTY ONLY — the events go to services/platform, which is ours. Any of these packages arriving would make `shared: false` false on this row, because a third-party analytics or attribution SDK transmits to its own vendor and that is precisely what Play's `shared` definition covers. It would also break the `required: false` claim, since none of them is gated on this app's consent controller.

answers.basis: OPTIONAL, and that is enforced rather than claimed. Collection is first-party only (no third-party analytics SDK exists in the dependency graph) and is gated on an explicit opt-in that defaults OFF: ConsentStatus.unknown is the launch state and is not consent (packages/core/lib/src/analytics/consent.dart:20-22), AnalyticsRecorder.log discards unless granted and does not buffer for replay, an unreadable consent store resolves to `unknown` rather than to consent, and withdrawal purges the queue and the disk key before the network call. Four events can actually fire: first_launch, app_open, return_visit and activation. Params are enumerable scalars only, capped at 12 keys and 64 characters — no free text and no user content. Under demo the whole rail is NoOpAnalytics and no consent prompt is shown at all.

There is no search field in the app, and no analytics event carries a query. Analytics params are enumerable values only (packages/core/lib/src/analytics/analytics.dart:64-90), so a search term could not travel even if a search existed.

No QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES and no package-listing dependency. The only <queries> element in the manifest is Flutter's default PROCESS_TEXT intent filter, which resolves a text-selection action and enumerates nothing.

The subscription NAME is free text the user types (add_subscription_sheet.dart:29). Under backend-live it is transmitted and stored in subly_db.subscriptions; under demo it stays in an in-memory list. Required — an app for tracking subscriptions cannot work without the subscription. The price and cycle from the same form are declared under Financial info > Other financial info; the same input is not double-counted, it is split by what each field IS.

Everything this app records about what a user does is the four funnel events, declared under App interactions. Nothing else about user behaviour is captured — there is no session replay, no interaction tracing (Sentry's enableUserInteractionTracing is left at its default of false) and no screenshot or view-hierarchy attachment.
There is no in-app browser and no WebView dependency. url_launcher is used only to hand four hardcoded nikatru.com legal URLs to the system browser, which returns nothing to the app.

🔴 THE ONE THING THE PLAY BUILD COLLECTS TODAY. The .aab lane passes --dart-define=GLITCHTIP_DSN, and TelemetryConfig.enabled is `dsn.isNotEmpty` — so on a trusted CI run the crash rail is ON in the shipping artefact and is its only network egress. REQUIRED: there is no opt-out in the app. Reports go to a self-hosted GlitchTip on Oracle Cloud, which is our own infrastructure and a service provider, so not `shared`. Before send: sendDefaultPii=false, enableAutoSessionTracking=false, and a beforeSend scrubber that redacts PAN, Aadhaar, email addresses, Indian mobile numbers and any run of >=10 digits out of the message, tags, extra, breadcrumb messages, breadcrumb data and exception values. ⚠️ The sink is NOT in tooling/legal/data-inventory.json because that register enumerates stores THIS REPOSITORY declares — D1 tables, KV namespaces and R2 buckets — and GlitchTip is an external service with no binding here. That is a real gap in the inventory's reach and it is recorded in `inventory.notInRegister` below rather than glossed.

Declared true rather than argued down. A crash event carries more than the stack: the SDK attaches device and OS context and lifecycle breadcrumbs by default, and those are NOT removed by scrubEvent, which reaches message, tags, extra, breadcrumbs and exceptions and does not touch event.contexts. 📌 THE CONTENTS ARE NO LONGER A 'WHATEVER IT CONTAINS' — this used to end by saying the identifier half was `null` under Device or other IDs and written up in `unresolved`. Both were settled on 2026-08-04 by reading the pinned SDK (see `resolved` and `crashSdkSurface`). sentry-android 8.51.0 DeviceInfoUtil.collectDeviceInformation sets manufacturer, brand, family, model, modelId, archs, chipset, orientation, simulator, screen width/height/density/dpi, boot time, timezone, locale, processor count/frequency and total memory — every one of which is diagnostic data leaving the device, so this answer stays `true`. The one field that is an IDENTIFIER rather than a characteristic is `device.id`, and it is now declared under Device or other IDs (true in both postures) rather than left open.

options.tracesSampleRate is set from TelemetryConfig, whose default is 0.01 (telemetry_config.dart:11), so roughly one launch in a hundred also sends a performance transaction. A sampled trace is still transmitted performance data; declaring 'no' because the rate is low would be a declaration about frequency, not about whether it happens.

clientAbsence.claim: 🔴 NEITHER IDENTIFIER IS AN ADVERTISING ID. The two this app transmits are a self-minted install UUID (`anon_id`) and the crash SDK's own install UUID (`contexts.device.id`) — both random, both per-install, both un-resettable-by-the-ad-framework and un-joinable to any ad network, because no ads or attribution SDK exists in the dependency graph. That sentence is the whole reason this row can be `shared: false` with purposes limited to Analytics and App functionality. Any tell below arriving would make it false at once, and would additionally require the AD_ID permission declaration and an 'Advertising or marketing' purpose on this form.

answers.basis:
TRUE IN BOTH POSTURES. Two independent contributions, and the second is the one that was `null`.

(1) anon_id — BACKEND-LIVE ONLY. A 128-bit random install identifier minted from Random.secure() and kept in shared_preferences under `nikatru.install_id`; it travels on every analytics and consent request. It is NOT an advertising ID and never has been — analytics_providers.dart:56 says 'Never a device ad-ID', the consent prompt tells the user in those words, and no ads or attribution SDK exists in the dependency graph.

(2) THE CRASH RAIL — BOTH POSTURES. 🔴 SETTLED 2026-08-04 BY READING THE SDK, NOT BY OBSERVING THE SINK. The recorded procedure was to build on CI, trigger a crash and inspect the stored event, on the stated ground that the payload 'is not derivable from source, because it is assembled inside the vendored SDK'. That ground was wrong: the vendored SDK IS source, it is pinned in pubspec.lock, and it is on disk in the pub cache. The chain, read end to end at the versions in `crashSdkSurface`:
  · sentry_flutter 9.26.0 lib/src/sentry_flutter_options.dart:34 — `autoInitializeNativeSdk = true` by default, and packages/telemetry does not override it, so the Android native SDK is initialised.
  · lib/src/sentry_flutter.dart:203-205 — LoadContextsIntegration is installed when `!platform.isWeb && native.supportsLoadContexts`; lib/src/native/sentry_native_channel.dart:135 makes that true for Android.
  · lib/src/integrations/load_contexts_integration.dart:172-174 — its event processor merges the native `contexts` map into `event.contexts` on every event.
  · sentry-android 8.51.0 DeviceInfoUtil.java:133-135 — `if (device.getId() == null) { device.setId(getDeviceId()); }`. The string `sendDefaultPii` DOES NOT OCCUR ANYWHERE in that 502-line file, so `options.sendDefaultPii = false` (telemetry_bootstrap.dart:42) does not suppress it. DeviceInfoUtil.java:492-500 resolves it to `Installation.id(context)`.
  · Installation.java:37-53 and 64-73 — a random UUID written once to a file named INSTALLATION in the app's files dir and read back on every later launch. STABLE FOR THE LIFE OF THE INSTALL.
  · It serialises under the key `id` (sentry-java Device.JsonKeys.ID). The Dart mirror does not model that key: sentry 9.26.0 lib/src/protocol/sentry_device.dart:195-226 sweeps unmodelled keys into `unknown`, and toJson() spreads `...?unknown` FIRST — so it round-trips to the sink verbatim rather than being dropped.
  · packages/telemetry/lib/src/telemetry_bootstrap.dart:84-139 — scrubEvent reaches message, tags, extra, breadcrumbs and exception values and never touches `event.contexts`, so nothing in this repository removes it.
A stable per-install identifier therefore leaves the device on every crash and on every sampled performance transaction, in the demo build as much as the live one, because GLITCHTIP_DSN is passed to both.

REQUIRED rather than optional: the crash-rail contribution has no user-facing opt-out and is present in every shipped posture. The anon_id half is consent-gated, and Play asks one answer per type, so the stricter of the two is the answer.

⚠️ THE ANSWER IS NOT UNIFORM ACROSS PLATFORMS, and this file governs the Play channel, so the Android column is the one that decides it. Android and iOS/macOS both attach a persistent per-install id — on Apple via sentry-cocoa 8.58.4 SentryClient.m:826, which calls setUserIdIfNoUserSet unconditionally inside prepareEvent, filling user.userId from SentryInstallation (SentryClient.m:979-988). Windows and Linux do NOT: factory_real.dart:14-15 selects the C binding, whose `supportsLoadContexts` is false (native/c/sentry_native.dart:149) and whose loadContexts() returns null (:152-155), so LoadContextsIntegration is never even installed, and the Dart-only IoEnricherEventProcessor fills name, processorCount, memorySize and freeMemory alone (sentry 9.26.0 io_enricher_event_processor.dart:41-48) — none of which identifies anything. Web is excluded by the same `!platform.isWeb` guard.

_resolved_why: 🔴 A SETTLED QUESTION KEEPS ITS WRITE-UP, OR THE NEXT PERSON RE-OPENS IT. Both entries below were
`unresolved` and both blocked the form. Deleting them on the day they were answered would leave two
answers whose reasoning lives only in a commit message, and the first thing anyone re-deriving a sworn
declaration does is ask why the value is what it is.
🔬 AND IT IS A CHECK, NOT A SCRAPBOOK. assert-play-declarations.mjs requires every type named in an
entry's `affects` to be NON-NULL in every posture, and refuses an id that appears in both lists.
Re-nulling an answer while leaving it listed as resolved fails the build — the exact shape of
backsliding that a prose-only record cannot catch, and the one this file would never print as blocking,
because the blocking list is built from `unresolved`.

resolved.question: Does the crash rail transmit anything that counts as a device identifier? sendDefaultPii=false stops the SDK attaching user.ip_address, but it does not disable the default `contexts.device` payload or the Sentry Android SDK's own installation id, and packages/telemetry's scrubEvent covers message, tags, extra, breadcrumbs and exceptions — not event.contexts.
resolved.answer: YES on Android (and on iOS/macOS). sentry-android 8.51.0 sets contexts.device.id to a UUID persisted in the app's files dir for the life of the install, ungated by sendDefaultPii; the Dart layer passes the unmodelled key through verbatim and scrubEvent never reaches contexts. Device or other IDs is therefore `true` under BOTH postures, and `required`, because the crash rail has no opt-out. NOT true on Windows or Linux, where the contexts integration is never installed at all.
resolved.settledBy: READING THE SDK SOURCE, which is what the superseded `howToResolve` said could not be done. It claimed the payload 'is not derivable from source, because it is assembled inside the vendored SDK' and prescribed a live crash against the GlitchTip instance instead. A vendored SDK is source: it is pinned in pubspec.lock and unpacked in the pub cache. The full file:line chain is in the Device or other IDs `basis`; the decisive line is DeviceInfoUtil.java:133-135 plus the fact that `sendDefaultPii` does not appear anywhere in that file. The live observation remains a fine CONFIRMATION and is strictly cheaper to do now that it knows what to look for — but it is no longer what the answer waits on.
resolved.coversOnly: The SDK-side payload. It does NOT establish what the GlitchTip server does with the event once received — see `crashSdkSurface.cannotSee`.

resolved.question: services/platform/src/routes/events.ts:118-126 stores country, region and city on every analytics row, read from Cloudflare's `request.cf` at the edge rather than from anything the app sends. Does Play's Data safety form count server-side geo inferred from the connection as the app collecting Approximate location?
resolved.answer: YES, and Play says so in one sentence: 'Approximate location that is inferred, such as via IP address or Access Point Name, must be disclosed here.' Because the derived value is also STORED (three columns on `events`) rather than used in flight, it is neither out of scope nor ephemeral. Declared collected under backend-live, optional, purpose Analytics, not shared.
resolved.settledBy: FINDING THE PRIMARY SOURCE THAT WAS RECORDED AS NOT EXISTING — on the page this file already cites. `sources.vocabulary` quotes support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/10787469 for the category list; the ruling sentence is a Note in the Approximate location row of that same table, and a second statement in the FAQ lower down covers IP-derived location directly. Both are now cited separately as sources.inferredLocation and sources.ipAddressUsage, so neither can be lost again by a re-fetch that only re-reads the paragraph already quoted.
resolved.coversOnly: The analytics rail, which is the only place this repository stores geo. It does NOT establish whether the self-hosted GlitchTip instance derives geo of its own from the connecting address — see `crashSdkSurface.cannotSee`. That could only ever affect the `demo` column, which is not the shipping posture.

_why: 🔴 THE DEVICE-ID ANSWER IS A FACT ABOUT A PINNED VERSION, NOT AN ETERNAL ONE. It was established by
reading sentry_flutter 9.26.0 and the sentry-android 8.51.0 it carries. Sentry ships often and Renovate
bumps this repository automatically, so the single most likely way that answer silently becomes false is
a dependency bump nobody connected to a store declaration. `pinned` is compared to the committed
pubspec.lock on every run: move the lock and the build fails asking for the reading to be redone.
⚠️ ONLY THE DART SIDE IS PINNABLE HERE. `transitiveNativeObserved` records the native SDK versions the
reading actually covered, but they come from sentry_flutter's own android/build.gradle and ios podspec —
files that are not in this repository — so they are an OBSERVATION with a date, not an assertion. They
are stated rather than omitted so that a future reader knows exactly which native source was read.
A bump of the Dart pin is the event that invalidates them, and that IS caught.

transitiveNativeObserved.readFrom: sentry_flutter-9.26.0/android/build.gradle:65 and sentry_flutter-9.26.0/ios/sentry_flutter.podspec:19, in the local pub cache

crashSdkSurface.finding: contexts.device.id is a stable per-install UUID on Android; it is NOT gated by sendDefaultPii and is NOT reached by packages/telemetry's scrubEvent. Windows and Linux attach no native contexts at all.
crashSdkSurface.cannotSee: ⚠️ WHAT THE GLITCHTIP SERVER DOES AFTER RECEIPT. Everything above is about the payload leaving the device. A Sentry-protocol server can enrich on ingest — most obviously by inferring geo from the connecting address — and the instance is self-hosted on Oracle Cloud with no configuration in this repository. That is why `Approximate location` under the `demo` posture rests on the analytics rail being off, and nothing else. It cannot affect the value typed into the console, because buildPosture.current is `backend-live`, where Approximate location is already true. Settling it means reading the GlitchTip instance's own configuration, not this tree.

encryptedInTransit.basis: Every endpoint the client can reach is https and the guard proves no `http://` string literal exists anywhere in the shipped Dart (apps/subly/lib, packages/*/lib). TLS terminates at the Cloudflare edge, provisioned by `custom_domain: true` in each Worker's wrangler config. No certificate pinning is used and tooling/ci/assert-no-tls-pinning.mjs keeps it that way.

deletionRequestSupported.basis: Both halves Play requires exist. In-app: Settings carries a delete-account control that re-authenticates with the password and calls DELETE /v1/account, and assert-deletion-control.mjs fails the build if any app that can create an account ships without one. Web: sites/nikatru/delete-account.html. Server: the erasure routes are derived from this file's `erasureRoutes`, which is itself derived from tooling/legal/data-inventory.json rather than typed here.
notReached: platform_db.events and platform_db.consent_artifacts are keyed on `anon_id` and there is NO anon_id -> user_id map anywhere ([ADR 020] forbids one being written), so an account deletion provably cannot address those rows. tooling/legal/data-inventory.json declares this as erasure kind `pseudonymous` and assert-data-inventory.mjs fails the day either table grows a user-shaped column. Play's account-deletion policy permits retention with disclosure; the inventory already records that privacy.html's wording is wider than what the route can do, under owner item O-3.

kv:nikatru-signups (the website launch-notification list) has erasure kind `no-route` — an operator deletes the key by hand, and sites/nikatru/delete-account.html says so. It is not written by this app and is excluded in `inventory.notFromThisApp`.

playFamiliesPolicy.basis: Subly is not designed for or targeted at children. The Play Console target-audience declaration and this badge are the same human's call and are recorded in content-rating.json; nothing in the tree can derive an intended audience.

independentSecurityReview.basis: No third-party MASVS assessment has been commissioned. The badge is optional and claiming it without a report would be a false statement to Google.

_why: 🔴 THIS IS THE LIMB THAT KEEPS THE FORM HONEST AS THE SCHEMA MOVES. tooling/legal/data-inventory.json
already enumerates every store this factory can put data in, both directions, and already fails when a
table appears with no row. This block makes the Data safety form the SAME system rather than a second
document that happens to agree today: every `personalData: true` row in that register is either mapped
to a declared-collected type by an `inventoryRows` entry above, or excluded here BY NAME with a reason.
A new personal-data table therefore fails TWO guards — one demanding a row, one demanding a Play answer
— and neither can be satisfied by prose.

notFromThisApp.table:platform_db.provider_notifications: The verbatim payment notification a provider POSTs to services/platform. It holds the buyer's name and email because that is what the provider sent; nothing leaves the device to produce it. No seller account exists (OWNER_QUEUE A-1) so nothing writes to it today.
notFromThisApp.table:platform_db.provider_accounts: Derived server-side from a provider notification. Same reasoning as provider_notifications.
notFromThisApp.table:platform_db.unclaimed_payments: Written when a payment arrives that cannot be attributed. Server-to-server from the provider; not transmitted by this app.
notFromThisApp.table:platform_db.cancellation_requests: Written by POST /v1/plan/cancel on the shared platform Worker. Subly has no cancel SURFACE — nothing in this app calls that route (the manage-plan screen that will arrives with P2.6a; nikatru_purchases became a dependency in P2.4b but has zero call sites). When the surface lands, this exclusion becomes false and must move into an answer row — the same rule that already moved table:platform_db.entitlements into the Purchase-history row with P2.4b.
notFromThisApp.kv:nikatru-signups: The nikatru.com launch-notification list, written by sites/nikatru/functions/api/subscribe.js from a form on the website. Not reachable from any app build.

notInRegister: THE CRASH SINK. GlitchTip (self-hosted, Oracle Cloud) receives crash and performance events from the shipping artefact and appears in NO row of data-inventory.json, because that register's three walks enumerate D1 tables, wrangler bindings and Pages-Function KV — an external service with no binding in this repository is outside all three. It is registered as a provider in tooling/legal/provider-register.json (row `oracle-cloud`), which is where the disclosure obligation is tracked, but the store-level 'what does it hold and for how long' question has no row anywhere. That is a real gap in the inventory's reach and it is written here rather than left for somebody to notice.

_why: PARSED OUT OF EVERY AndroidManifest.xml IN THE APP, WITH XML COMMENTS STRIPPED FIRST, and compared
for EQUALITY in both directions. A permission is the single loudest tell that a data type just
started being collected, and the mistake this repository keeps recording is a scanner that stops
scanning — so this is an equality, not a subset: a permission appearing OR disappearing fails, and
the fix is to say which Play data type it changes.
The main (release) manifest declares NONE. The debug and profile manifests declare INTERNET, which
Flutter's tooling needs for hot reload and which is not merged into a release build.
androidPermissions.cannotSee: ⚠️ THE MERGED MANIFEST. Gradle merges permissions contributed by every plugin's own AndroidManifest.xml, and none of those files is in this repository. Reading the locked plugin set, the expected additions are VIBRATE and POST_NOTIFICATIONS (flutter_local_notifications) and INTERNET / ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE (the sentry-android AAR pulled in by sentry_flutter) — none of which is a collection signal on its own. That set was NOT read from a built artefact and is not asserted anywhere: Android cannot be built on the maintainer's machine, and the guard says so on every run instead of pretending. To settle it, run `bundletool dump manifest` on a CI-built .aab. What the guard CAN do about it is `dependencySurface` below — a permission-bearing plugin cannot arrive without a new dependency, and a new dependency fails the build.

_why: 🔴 THE MECHANISM BY WHICH A DATA-COLLECTING SDK ACTUALLY ARRIVES. Nobody adds ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION
to a manifest by hand; they add `geolocator` to a pubspec and Gradle merges the permission in from a
file this repository does not contain. So the DIRECT dependency set of apps/subly is declared here
and compared for equality: a package appearing with no entry fails with 'a new dependency arrived and
nobody said what data it can collect', and an entry for a package that is gone fails too.
⚠️ DIRECT ONLY, AND THE LIMIT IS STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN. Transitive packages are not enumerated:
the resolved graph churns on every Renovate bump and an equality over it would be noise that gets
switched off. A transitive SDK still has to be pulled by one of the direct entries below, each of
which is either first-party or a package whose purpose is named here.

nikatru_core.why: First-party. Domain models, the Result type, the analytics recorder and the consent controller — no I/O of its own; every transport is injected.

nikatru_api_client.why: First-party. The Dio transports that actually send subscriptions, budget, analytics events and the consent artifact. It is the package through which everything declared collected under backend-live leaves the device.

nikatru_design_system.why: First-party. Tokens, theming and widgets. No network, no storage.

nikatru_platform_storage.why: First-party. shared_preferences and flutter_secure_storage adapters. Writes ON the device only — nothing here transmits.

nikatru_auth_supabase.why: First-party. Wires the Supabase session through OS-backed secure storage so the refresh token is not written in plaintext. Under demo it is never initialised (main.dart:58 gates on isSupabaseConfigured).

nikatru_telemetry.why: First-party wrapper over sentry_flutter. THE ONLY THING THAT TRANSMITS IN THE DEMO POSTURE, and the source of the unresolved device-context question.

dio.why: HTTP client. A transport, not a collector — what travels over it is declared by the api_client entry above.

supabase_flutter.why: The identity SDK. Sends the email and password to Supabase GoTrue and returns the session. Inert under demo, where MockAuthRepository is selected instead.

nikatru_notifications.why: First-party wrapper (packages/notifications) over the flutter_local_notifications + timezone pair already declared below — [13]T-9 routes the retention-touch attribution through it so a tap is attributable to its reminder. It schedules LOCAL notifications only: no new permission, no network, no data category beyond what its two wrapped deps (both already in this surface) declare. Added 2026-08-08 with PR #195 under [ADR 036].

flutter_local_notifications.why: Schedules renewal reminders ON THE DEVICE. Nothing is sent anywhere — there is no push service, no token registration and no Firebase. It is the source of the merged VIBRATE and POST_NOTIFICATIONS permissions.

timezone.why: Local timezone database for scheduling the reminders above. Offline data, no I/O.

intl.why: Number formatting. Subly's entire use is one NumberFormat in lib/core/format/currency.dart.

url_launcher.why: Hands four hardcoded nikatru.com legal URLs to the system browser. The app receives nothing back and learns nothing about what the browser does.

package_info_plus.why: Reads the app's OWN version and build number from the OS package manager — input to the CFG-1 force-update kill-switch comparison. No personal data, no network. Added 2026-08-08 with productization P2.4a under [ADR 037].

nikatru_purchases.why: First-party client rail (packages/purchases) for the money rail: offerings, entitlement state and convergence ([5]M-8), fetched over the api_client/dio transports already declared above and keyed to the authenticated account — so its data categories (User IDs, the entitlement read now declared under Financial info > Purchase history) are carried by entries and answer rows, not new here, hence introduces []. It contains NO checkout: purchase execution happens on the apex web page ([ADR 038]) in a browser, and no billing SDK or payment instrument exists in this codebase (see the Purchase-history row's clientAbsence). Zero call sites at the time of writing — the first caller lands with the chassis money surfaces (P2.6a) and the paywall flip is Phase 4. Added 2026-08-08 with productization P2.4b under [ADR 037]; the Purchase-history answer row moved in the same commit because that row's tells named this package in advance, exactly so the two could never move separately.

flutter_localizations.why: The SDK localization package driving gen-l10n from lib/l10n/*.arb. Offline string tables, no I/O. Added 2026-08-08 with productization P2.4a under [ADR 037].
